title: security: RBAC v2 - enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening for Private
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Enforce KMS region pinning for Private deployments; audit events now include kms_region and residency_reason for key/material access attempts; DB migration to add kms_residency column. Backwards-compatible with feature-flag off for 1 release.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments previously allowed service accounts in a cluster to reference KMS keys without a final residency enforcement check. This PR hardens RBAC v2 by enforcing KMS region pinning at the policy evaluation layer and surfaces richer audit events for downstream compliance.

Summary of changes: Checklist:
- [x] Enforce kms_region pinning in RBAC policy evaluation (runtime check)
- [x] Emit audit events with kms_region and residency_reason for must-generate audit trails
- [x] DB migration to persist kms_residency on secrets and keys for historical auditing
- [x] CLI/operator validation in private-installer to surface residency violations early
- [x] Backfill tool + migration test harness for existing customers (opt-in)
- [x] Unit + integration tests and e2e test for private-installer workflow
- [ ] Docs: operator guide (follow-up PR planned)

Notes: Enforcement is gated behind a cluster feature-flag (rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce) enabled by default in new Private installs and off for upgrade paths; audit logging is always on. This approach keeps rolling upgrades safe while allowing observers to validate events before enforcement. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-3489, SEC-122, SUP-9012.

Risk & rollout plan: Migration adds a nullable kms_residency column; the backfill is an opt-in job to avoid windows of heavy DBA load. We will ship with audits for 2 weeks on a canary fleet before enabling enforcement cluster-wide. If unexpected errors occur, enforcement can be toggled off per-cluster via feature flag.
